prompt: We need to decide how to handle background jobs in our Rails app. We've been using Sidekiq with Redis but our ops team hates managing Redis and we're looking at switching to GoodJob (which uses Postgres) or Que (also Postgres-backed). GoodJob has a nice UI and active maintenance, Que is simpler but less actively developed. Our main drivers are: ops simplicity (no extra infra), reliability, and team familiarity with Postgres. We're leaning toward GoodJob. Write the ADR.

assertions.description: File has YAML frontmatter with title, adr, status, date, authors, and changelog fields
Document contains Motivation, Decision Drivers, Options, and Decision sections
Each option lists pros and cons referencing the same named decision drivers
Document includes a Consequences section with at least one good and one bad consequence
ADR file is at docs/adrs/NNNN-*.md with zero-padded number and kebab-case name
docs/adrs/README.md exists and contains a table entry linking to the new ADR
Options section contains at least one specific current fact (version number, release date, GitHub activity, or recent changelog note) that goes beyond the user's original description
